question: What changed for facility-001 between June 10, 2021 and March 23, 2023 concerning the scheduled aluminum row and progress reports? answer: The 2021 permit provided report-only monthly aluminum results for three years, then a scheduled 87 µg/L monthly-average limit, with January 15 progress reports and a reopener. A January 4, 2023 request followed the November 12, 2021 state revision and September 15, 2022 EPA approval. The retained statement of basis proposes removing the row and schedule; the issued March 23 modification visibly strikes them out, with footnote 12 changed to N/A. This prevents treating the extracted struck-out 87 as a surviving limit or letting it mature automatically in 2024. It does not establish historical sample compliance or removal of unrelated conditions. The separate WET-associated effluent aluminum analysis remains report mg/L once per quarter by composite sample; ambient aluminum remains quarterly grab sampling of receiving water immediately upstream of the discharge zone of influence. These separate table/footnote 16–17 duties are not the deleted twice-monthly row.

question: Follow facility-001’s joint operator/owner identity into the nitrogen annual-report condition and the limited 2023 modification. Register the report clock and the additional content triggered by an annual increase.

A report obligation does not prove an increase occurred or establish a numeric nitrogen effluent cap.

question: For facility-003, register the new chemical/additive notification pathway and minimum supporting information. Can a new additive be discharged immediately merely because aluminum monitoring was deleted?
answer: Undisclosed chemicals/substitutions are prohibited. Previously disclosed discharge is limited to the disclosed frequency and level and must meet the cited conditions. A new chemical is authorized 30 days after written EPA notification unless EPA otherwise notifies. Supply identity/manufacturer, purpose, SDS/CAS/registration where applicable, application frequency/magnitude/duration/method, maximum discharge concentration and available toxicity, plus rationale addressing existing and potentially needed limits. The aluminum deletion does not change this independent notification condition or prove a particular additive was approved.

evidence.quote: 4. Discharges of Chemicals and Additives The discharge of any chemical or additive, including chemical substitution that was not reported in the application submitted to EPA or provided through a subsequent written notification submitted to EPA is prohibited. Upon the effective date of this permit, chemicals and/or additives that have been disclosed to EPA may be discharged up to the frequency and level disclosed, provided that such discharge does not violate §§ 307 or 311 of the CWA or applicable State water quality standards. Discharges of a new chemical or additive are authorized under this permit 30 days following written notification to EPA unless otherwise notified by EPA. To request authorization to discharge a new chemical or additive, the Permittee must submit a written notification to EPA in accordance with Part I.D.3 of this permit. The written notification must include the following information, at a minimum: a. The following information for each chemical and/or additive that will be discharged: (1) Product name, chemical formula, general description, and manufacturer of the chemical/additive; (2) Purpose or use of the chemical/additive; (3) Safety Data Sheet (SDS), Chemical Abstracts Service (CAS) Registry number, and EPA registration number, if applicable, for each chemical/additive; (4) The frequency (e.g., daily), magnitude (i.e., maximum application concentration), duration (e.g., hours), and method of application for the chemical/additive; (5) The maximum discharge concentration; and (6) The vendor's reported aquatic toxicity, if available (i.e., NOAEL and/or LC50 in percent for aquatic organism(s)).

question: Evaluate a facility-003 acquisition finding that assigns 152 or 515 µg/L as the new approved effluent limit after deleting 87. Distinguish calculation, criterion and issued scope.
answer: The basis compares estimated downstream 152 µg/L with watershed-default criterion 515 µg/L and finds no reasonable potential, proposing removal of the scheduled 87 µg/L row and schedule. The issued March 23 action implements visible deletion, not a replacement 152/515 effluent cap. Do not import Laurel’s 158 estimate or imply all pollutants compliant, current authorization beyond expiry or an unrestricted operational waiver. Ask for later applicable permits and actual monitoring/compliance evidence.

As a result, the Modified Permit proposes to remove the monthly average aluminum limit of 87 µg/L. Additionally, the compliance schedule included in Part I.C.6 of the 2021 Permit is unnecessary and will be removed from the final Modified Permit. 3.0
